Alright, buckle up, buttercup. It's Thursday, November 26, 2026, and your favorite news-junkie-slash-hot-take-machine is here to drop the daily download. Forget the turkey coma, the real feast is in these headlines.

***

Money Talk

- **Trump claims "record setting error" on GDP.**
  President Trump is fuming over a massive upward revision to Q3 GDP data, calling it a "mistake" and demanding an "immediate investigation." Because, you know, good economic news *must* be fake if it doesn't fit the narrative. [S1][S16]
- **Semiconductor chips officially the new black gold.**
  For the first time ever, semiconductor exports have blown past oil and gas in 2026, driven by insatiable AI demand. If you're not investing in silicon, you're missing the next era of resource wars. [S3]
- **Spain's de Cos to helm European Central Bank.**
  Pablo Hernández de Cos, former Bank of Spain governor, is set to take the reins at the ECB, succeeding Christine Lagarde. He's walking into a political minefield with choppy growth ahead – good luck, pal. [S5][S15]
- **UK road projects axed for defense spending.**
  Two major East Midlands road schemes, including A38 upgrades, are getting shelved. £400m diverted to defense. Regional mayors are calling it "disappointing and short-sighted," probably because they still have to drive on those roads. [S11]
- **Norse Atlantic teeters on the brink of collapse.**
  The airline has suspended all flights and is desperately seeking urgent funding to avoid bankruptcy. Another one bites the dust in the hyper-competitive world of budget air travel. [S9]

World Lore

- **North Korea's Kim doubles down on nukes.**
  Kim Jong Un is reportedly visiting nuclear ingredient facilities, vowing to build more weapons to counter threats from the U.S. and South Korea. So, same old song, just louder bass. [S22]
- **Trump "urged Putin to pull back" in Europe.**
  President Trump claims he talked to Putin about de-escalating military aggression in Europe and believes a deal between Russia and Ukraine is possible. Because a quick chat is all it takes, apparently. [S34]
- **Congo Ebola outbreak hits 12,000 cases amidst fighting.**
  The fast-moving Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo is now at 12,000 cases, with conflict between rebels and the army actively messing up containment efforts. It’s a tragic reminder that geopolitics doesn't pause for pandemics. [S21]
- **Trial begins for alleged Russian spy in Berlin.**
  A Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia, using her military contacts to funnel German defense info and Ukraine intel, is finally facing trial after health delays. Talk about a holiday buzzkill. [S31]
- **Iraqi Kurdistan protests Baghdad's oil takeover.**
  Thousands are demonstrating in Iraqi Kurdistan's capital, pushing back against Baghdad's plans to seize control of oil operations and border crossings. More internal friction in a region that really doesn't need it. [S35]

Tech Tea

- **Musk's SpaceX gets green light for orbital AI data centers.**
  The FCC has approved Elon Musk’s ambitious plan to launch one million Starmind satellites for in-space data processing. Supporters tout energy efficiency, but expect some celestial traffic jams. [S13][S45]
- **X finally adds parental controls after two decades.**
  Elon Musk's social network X (formerly Twitter) has *finally* introduced parental controls for teenagers. Only took twenty years to realize kids might be on the internet. Better late than never, I guess? [S41]
- **S&P eyes Nvidia downgrade over "key man" risks.**
  Credit rating agency S&P is considering lowering Nvidia's credit rating, citing governance concerns and "key man" risks. Even chip titans aren't immune to scrutiny, especially when they're essentially the new oil. [S44]
- **Android devs forced to dox themselves.**
  Google is requiring independent Android app developers to publicly share their phone number and address starting next year, citing EU regulations. Privacy concerns are, understandably, through the roof. [S48]
- **AI turns Thanksgiving sous-chef (and maybe therapist).**
  From cookbooks to YouTube to ChatGPT, AI is now officially in the kitchen, helping plan holiday menus. Just make sure your chatbot isn't trying to replace Grandma's secret recipe for passive aggression. [S19]

Creator Szn

- **Brands desperately trying to score creator content.**
  As social trends move faster than a TikTok dance challenge, brands like General Mills are trying to systematize how they measure a creator's post for "shareability." Good luck quantifying organic buzz, marketing folks. [S56]
- **Dick's Sporting Goods enters ad game with youth sports.**
  Dick's is betting big on youth sports, turning its GameChanger platform into a premium ad business. Monetizing pee-wee leagues? That's a bold play, Cotton. [S57]
- **The "clipping economy" faces platform crackdown.**
  The wild west of content clipping is getting tamed as platforms tighten up, forcing creators to rethink how they manage and control their bite-sized content. Time to get creative or get sued. [S59]
- **AI is shaping holiday shopping research.**
  Shoppers are increasingly turning to AI for product research ahead of Black Friday, leaving marketers scrambling to figure out how to pivot. If your AI isn't recommending the perfect gadget, it's not doing its job. [S60]
- **New customer acquisition is holiday season's top priority.**
  With Black Friday Cyber Monday upon us, brands like A-Frame and Ritual are laser-focused on reeling in new customers. It's a crowded market out there, so expect your inbox to be a war zone. [S58]

Supply Lines

- **UPS acquires Smartways Logistics to boost healthcare footprint.**
  UPS is making a big move in Australia and New Zealand's healthcare logistics sector by acquiring Smartways Logistics. This deal adds couriers reaching ~1,300 hospitals daily, seriously expanding UPS's specialized delivery network down under. [S76][S77][S78][S79]
- **FedEx MD-11 overshoots Miami runway.**
  A FedEx cargo jet ran off the runway at Miami airport on Thanksgiving Eve, ending up in a grassy field. Déjà vu for Miami, and definitely not the kind of "special delivery" anyone wants. [S61][S85]
- **DHL partners across Africa to empower SMEs.**
  DHL is making serious moves in Africa, teaming up with Equity Bank to support SMEs in five African markets, engaging with Ghana's Trade Minister, and partnering with the Chinese Chamber to boost Nigeria-China trade. Talk about a multimodal efficiency play. [S80][S81][S82][S83][S84]
- **Ex-Convoy CEO's new startup raises $277 million in stealth.**
  The former Convoy CEO's new logistics startup has emerged from stealth mode with a massive $277 million in funding. Another big player is entering the freight tech arena, signaling continued innovation (and probably more disruption). [S96]
- **Ocean freight rates still double last year, congestion lingers.**
  DHL reports ocean rates are still 138% higher than 2025, with 3.6 million TEUs stuck in congestion. Shippers are prioritizing resilience over price for the 2027 RFQ season, because nobody wants a repeat of the past few years. [S63]
- **Nvidia halts server shipments to parts of Asia due to US export rules.**
  New US export controls have caused Nvidia to tell manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This could seriously impact airfreight for high-value tech goods. [S71]
- **Cargo crime gangs exploit staffing shortages for holiday heists.**
  Verisk CargoNet warns that criminals are infiltrating US haulage firms by posing as drivers and dispatchers to steal shipments, with data center hardware and metals being prime targets. Staffing shortages are making the industry a juicy target for these patient planners. [S72]

Speed Round

- Donald Trump pledges two SpaceX shares for every child in America, an $18 billion giveaway.
- Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for the first time ever due to an impending nor'easter.
- An East Coast storm is disrupting Thanksgiving travel and could cause coastal flooding.
- Federal judge blocks the FCC from reviewing ABC's licenses early, upholding free speech.
- Elon Musk's MacBook Neo and Garmin Forerunner are seeing rare Black Friday discounts.
- PETA alleges animal abuse in PepsiCo’s sugar sourcing supply chain.
- The EU Court is putting Amazon-style delivery networks in its regulatory crosshairs.
